idea.name: 24h Breakout, 12h Exit
idea.hypothesis: Breakouts above a recent range may capture persistent repricing as market participants adjust positions; a shorter trailing-channel exit aims to cut failed breakouts while letting sustained moves run. The different entry and exit windows should generate repeated trades rather than simply holding through the period.
idea.rules: After each completed one-minute bar t, using only earlier completed bars, enter if flat and close[t] > 1.003 × max(high[t−1440:t−1]). Exit if long and close[t] < min(low[t−720:t−1]). Submit the resulting market order for the next bar’s open; do not act on a signal using the same bar’s fill. On entry, buy BTC using 95% of available USDT including the 0.1% fee and 0.02% slippage reserve; do not add while long. On exit, sell the entire BTC holding. Apply the 10%-of-bar-volume fill cap; cancel any unfilled entry remainder, and continue submitting exit orders on subsequent bars until flat. Stay flat until a new entry signal. idea.name: 4h Range Breakout
idea.hypothesis: BTC breakouts can attract persistent follow-on order flow as traders react to new price highs; waiting for a completed-bar close above the range may filter some intrabar noise. A shorter trailing exit aims to cut failed breakouts while retaining sustained moves.
idea.rules: Aggregate the observed one-minute bars into UTC 4-hour bars. At each completed 4-hour bar, if flat and its close is above the highest high of the preceding six completed 4-hour bars and above its own open, enter long at the next one-minute bar's open. While long, exit at the next one-minute open after a completed 4-hour bar closes below the lowest low of the preceding two completed 4-hour bars. Evaluate signals only at 4-hour closes; do not pyramid or re-enter until a later completed bar gives a fresh entry signal. Use all available cash for each entry, sizing BTC so the purchase and fee fit the cash balance; sell the entire holding on exit. idea.name: Filtered 48-Hour Breakout
idea.hypothesis: BTC can exhibit multi-day trend persistence as information, spot flows, and liquidation-driven moves are absorbed gradually. A 48-hour breakout with a broader short-term trend filter aims to capture those sustained moves while avoiding frequent trading and its fees.
idea.rules: Aggregate the observed one-minute bars into UTC-aligned 4-hour candles. After each completed candle, when flat, enter long for the next one-minute open if its close is above the highest high of the preceding 12 completed 4-hour candles (excluding the current candle) and EMA(6) is above EMA(18), both calculated on 4-hour closes. While long, exit at the next one-minute open if a completed 4-hour close is below EMA(6), or at/below the highest 4-hour close since entry minus 2.5 × ATR(14); ATR is the simple mean of 14 true ranges on completed 4-hour candles. Do not re-enter until a later completed candle produces a fresh entry signal. At entry, submit a market order sized to use 95% of available USDT at the expected fill price; at exit, sell the entire filled position. Use only completed candles for signals, and apply the specified next-bar execution, fees, slippage, latency, and volume cap; cancel any unfilled remainder.

idea.name: Hourly Channel Breakout
idea.hypothesis: Medium-term price momentum may persist because large BTC moves attract follow-on flows, while a slower breakout rule can avoid much of the churn that makes one-minute signals costly. A long-only channel strategy tests this with relatively infrequent entries and exits.

idea.name: Trend-Filtered Flush Reversal
idea.hypothesis: A sharp, unusually high-volume selloff can reflect urgent liquidity demand or stop-driven selling that temporarily pushes BTC below fair value. When flat, define the flush condition as (a) close is at least 1.2% below the close 60 bars earlier, (b) volume summed over the latest 60 bars is at least 1.8 times the median volume of the previous 168 completed UTC-hour bars, and (c) the latest completed hourly close is above the simple average of the latest 200 completed hourly closes. Enter at the next bar's open on the first bar where the condition changes from false to true; do not re-enter until it has first become false again. Buy with all available cash, subject to the simulator's fill cap. After the entry fill, exit at the next bar's open if any of these holds: the current bar's low is at or below 1.0% below the fill price, its high is at or above 1.5% above the fill price, six hours have elapsed, or the latest completed hourly close is at or below the 200-hour average. If both price thresholds are touched in one bar, treat the stop as triggered. Apply the specified fees, slippage, latency, and volume cap to every fill.

idea.name: Selloff Absorption Reversal
idea.hypothesis: A rapid, unusually high-volume selloff can reflect clustered stops or liquidations rather than lasting new information. idea.name: Trend-Gated Flush Reversion

idea.name: Liquidation Shock Reversion
idea.hypothesis: A sharp, high-volume BTC selloff can reflect forced liquidation and temporary liquidity imbalance rather than lasting information; as patient buyers absorb the flow, some of the move may reverse. idea.name: Volatility-Targeted BTC
idea.hypothesis: BTC volatility clusters, so recent realized volatility can help size exposure: reducing position size in high-volatility regimes may limit drawdowns without requiring directional signals or frequent attempts to time reversals. Daily rebalancing makes this a genuinely active risk-management strategy rather than a rarely triggered buy-and-hold filter.
idea.rules: Use only completed 1-minute bars. After the last completed bar of each UTC day, calculate annualized realized volatility from the preceding 10,080 close-to-close returns: σ = sqrt(525,600 × mean(r²)). Until that full history is available, remain in cash. Set target BTC weight to min(1, 0.50/σ), with no leverage. Compare this target with the BTC share of account equity at the latest close; if the target is below 5%, exit the position, otherwise rebalance only when the difference is at least 5 percentage points. Size the order to reach the target weight using equity at that close, and execute at the next bar’s open, subject to the stated fee, slippage, latency, and 10%-of-bar-volume cap. Do not carry unfilled order quantity forward; reassess at the next daily rebalance.

idea.name: Daily Volatility Scaling
idea.hypothesis: Bitcoin volatility clusters, so a fixed full-size position can expose the account to unusually large losses during turbulent periods. Daily inverse-volatility sizing aims to reduce that exposure when realized volatility rises without trying to predict short-term price direction.
idea.rules: At 00:00 UTC each day, compute the standard deviation of the previous 336 completed hourly close-to-close log returns and annualize it as sigma = hourly_std * sqrt(8760). Set the target BTC weight to min(1, 0.70 / sigma). Using account equity and the latest available price, rebalance toward that weight at the next one-minute bar's open only if the target differs from the current BTC weight by at least 5 percentage points. Buy only with available cash; sell no more BTC than held. Apply the stated fees, slippage, latency, and 10%-of-bar-volume fill cap; cancel any unfilled remainder and reassess at the next daily rebalance.

idea.name: Downside-Volatility Budget
idea.hypothesis: BTC volatility clusters, and unusually high downside volatility can signal elevated near-term crash risk even when direction is uncertain. Scaling spot exposure to a downside-risk budget may reduce losses in stressed periods while retaining more exposure in calmer periods; this is a risk-management hypothesis, not a guarantee of higher returns.
idea.rules: Use only completed one-minute close-to-close returns. At each UTC 4-hour boundary, calculate downside volatility from the preceding 1,440 returns as v = sqrt(525600 × mean(min(r, 0)^2)), where r is the simple return and v is annualized. Set target BTC exposure to clamp(0.45 / v, 0, 1) of marked account equity; if v is zero, target 100%. Stay in cash until the full lookback is available. Submit a rebalance after the signal bar closes, filling no earlier than the next bar's open. Rebalance only if target exposure differs from actual exposure by more than 10 percentage points of equity; otherwise hold. Buy with available cash or sell held BTC to reach the target, never borrow or sell more than held, and apply the stated fees, slippage, latency, and 10%-of-bar-volume cap.

idea.name: Volatility Regime Filter
idea.hypothesis: BTC volatility clusters, so elevated realized volatility can signal a persistently turbulent regime with greater downside and execution risk. A hysteretic volatility filter tests whether stepping aside in that regime improves risk-adjusted results without relying on breakout or selloff-reversal signals.
idea.rules: Aggregate the one-minute bars into UTC hourly closes. At each completed hour, calculate realized volatility as the square root of the sum of squared log returns over the latest 48 hourly bars. Compare it with the 45th and 55th percentiles of the preceding 720 hourly realized-volatility readings, excluding the current reading. If flat and volatility is at or below the 45th percentile, buy; if long and it is at or above the 55th percentile, sell all. Otherwise retain the current position. Start flat after the warm-up period. Use all available cash for entries; submit orders for the next one-minute bar's open and apply the stated fee, slippage, latency, and volume-cap rules.

idea.name: Weekday Exposure

After the Friday 23:59 bar closes, submit a market sell for all BTC held; fill at the next bar’s open. Hold no BTC over the weekend. Apply the stated fees, slippage, and 10%-of-bar-volume cap; cancel any unfilled remainder and do not chase it. Repeat weekly.

idea.name: Weekday-Only BTC

idea.name: Session-Overlap Continuation

idea.name: Flow-Confirmed Trend
idea.hypothesis: Persistent positive volume-weighted buying pressure may indicate informed or urgent demand that continues after it appears in the bars. Requiring price to remain above a short trend baseline aims to avoid following positive-looking candle flow during a broader decline; this is a testable order-flow hypothesis, not a claim of established edge.
idea.rules: For each completed one-minute bar, estimate signed volume as V × (2C − H − L)/(H − L), using zero when H = L. Let F120 be the sum of signed volume over the last 120 bars divided by their total volume; calculate F30 similarly over 30 bars, and an EMA of the last 240 closes. When flat, enter long if F120 > 0.20 and the close is above the EMA. When long, exit if the close is below the EMA, or if F30 < −0.15 on 10 consecutive completed bars. Submit each decision after the signal bar and execute at the next bar’s open; cancel any unfilled remainder after that bar and retry on later bars only while the relevant condition still holds. On entry, target the maximum BTC affordable with available cash, including fees; never borrow or sell more than held.
